title: Module 12 · PICU and Pediatric Emergencies
intro: The adult ceiling, PALS doses, adenosine and atropine, status epilepticus with ESETT, pediatric DKA and cerebral edema, RSI, withdrawal weans, fluids and dosing anchors, and poisonings.

cases.title: The adult ceiling
cases.stem: A 15 year old, 82 kg. Order: acetaminophen 15 mg/kg PO every 6 hours = 1,230 mg.

steps.q: What is wrong?

options.t: Pediatric mg/kg doses never exceed the adult dose: cap at 1,000 mg per dose and 4 g per day

options.why: 1,230 mg is above the adult single dose.

steps.q: Which other pediatric checks run on every order?

options.t: Measured weight in kg, and actual vs ideal weight for obese children per drug
Standard concentration in the pump library and a measurable volume

cases.pearl: **mg/kg, but never above the adult dose.**

cases.title: Pediatric arrest
cases.stem: A 20 kg child in asystole. IO in place.

steps.q: Epinephrine dose?

options.t: 0.01 mg/kg = 0.2 mg = 2 mL of 0.1 mg/mL, every 3 to 5 minutes (max 1 mg)
options.why: PALS 2025: as early as possible in nonshockable rhythms.
Same mg, but use the 0.1 mg/mL concentration to avoid errors.

steps.q: Rhythm changes to VF, refractory to shocks. Amiodarone?

options.t: 5 mg/kg = 100 mg, may repeat up to 15 mg/kg total

cases.pearl: **PALS epi 0.01 mg/kg (0.1 mL/kg of 0.1 mg/mL). Amio 5 mg/kg.**

sources.t: AHA/AAP 2025 Pediatric Advanced Life Support (AHA CPR and ECC 2025, Part 8)

cases.title: Pediatric SVT and bradycardia
cases.stem: Two children: (A) 15 kg with SVT at 260, stable; (B) 10 kg with bradycardia from AV block.

steps.q: Adenosine for A?

options.t: 0.1 mg/kg = 1.5 mg rapid push with flush (max 6 mg); second dose 0.2 mg/kg (max 12 mg)

steps.q: Atropine for B?

options.t: 0.02 mg/kg = 0.2 mg IV (max single dose 0.5 mg)

sources.t: AHA/AAP 2025 Pediatric Advanced Life Support (AHA CPR and ECC 2025, Part 8)

cases.title: Status epilepticus in a child
cases.stem: A 25 kg child seizing for 8 minutes. No IV yet.

steps.q: First line without IV access?

options.t: Midazolam IM 5 mg (13 to 40 kg), single dose
options.why: AES 2016. Intranasal or buccal midazolam and rectal diazepam are other options.

steps.q: IV placed, still seizing 5 minutes later. Lorazepam dose?

options.t: 0.1 mg/kg = 2.5 mg IV (max 4 mg), may repeat once
4 mg because that is the max

steps.q: Still seizing at 20 minutes. Second line options (ESETT: similar efficacy)?

options.t: Fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg (500 mg PE, max 1,500 mg PE)
Valproate 40 mg/kg (1,000 mg, max 3,000 mg), avoiding it in suspected mitochondrial or liver disease

options.why: Benzodiazepines lose effect as seizures continue.

cases.pearl: **SE: benzo (IM midaz 5 or 10 mg, or lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg), then levetiracetam, fosphenytoin or valproate.**

sources.t: Glauser T, et al. AES guideline: treatment of convulsive status epilepticus in children and adults. Epilepsy Curr 2016;16:48-61
Kapur J, et al. Randomized trial of three anticonvulsant medications for status epilepticus (ESETT). N Engl J Med 2019;381:2103-2113

cases.title: Pediatric DKA
cases.stem: A 30 kg child in DKA. K 4.2.

steps.q: Insulin plan?

options.t: 0.05 to 0.1 units/kg/h IV (1.5 to 3 units/h), no bolus, started after the first hour of fluids

steps.q: What emergency do you prepare for?

options.t: Cerebral edema: mannitol 0.5 to 1 g/kg over 10 to 15 minutes or 3% saline 2.5 to 5 mL/kg at the bedside
options.why: Warning signs: headache, falling heart rate, rising BP, altered mental status.
The main cause of DKA death in children.

steps.q: How do pediatric and adult potassium cutoffs differ?

options.t: Adults: hold insulin until K is 3.5 or more (2024 consensus). Children: replace potassium first if low; many protocols use 3.3; follow St. Mary's

cases.pearl: **Peds DKA: no bolus, 0.05 to 0.1 units/kg/h, mannitol or 3% ready.**

sources.t: Glaser N, et al. ISPAD 2022 consensus guidelines: DKA and HHS. Pediatr Diabetes 2022;23:835-856

cases.title: Pediatric RSI
cases.stem: A 12 kg toddler in septic shock needs intubation.

steps.q: Which induction agent fits septic shock?

options.why: Many protocols avoid etomidate in septic shock (adrenal suppression).

steps.q: Paralytic?

options.t: Succinylcholine in a child with suspected muscular dystrophy

cases.title: Iatrogenic withdrawal
cases.setting: PICU · day 9 of fentanyl and midazolam
cases.stem: A child extubated after 9 days of fentanyl and midazolam infusions is irritable, sweaty, with diarrhea and tremors.

steps.q: What is this?

options.t: Iatrogenic opioid and benzodiazepine withdrawal (expected after 5 or more days of infusions)

options.why: Consider it, but the pattern fits withdrawal.

steps.q: What is the pharmacist role?

options.t: Write a wean plan, often with enteral methadone and lorazepam, and taper with scores

cases.pearl: **5+ days of drips: expect withdrawal. WAT-1 and a wean.**

cases.title: Everyday pediatric doses and fluids
cases.stem: A 20 kg child admitted for dehydration.

steps.q: Maintenance fluid rate by Holliday Segar (4/2/1)?

options.t: 60 mL/h: 40 for the first 10 kg + 20 for the next 10 kg

steps.q: Which fluid does AAP 2018 recommend for most hospitalized children?

options.t: Isotonic fluid with appropriate potassium and dextrose

steps.q: Acetaminophen and ibuprofen doses for 20 kg?

options.t: Acetaminophen 300 mg every 6 hours (15 mg/kg); ibuprofen 200 mg every 6 to 8 hours (10 mg/kg)

cases.pearl: **4/2/1, isotonic fluids, APAP 15 mg/kg, ibuprofen 10 mg/kg.**

sources.t: Feld LG, et al. AAP clinical practice guideline: maintenance IV fluids in children. Pediatrics 2018;142:e20183083

cases.title: Pediatric poisonings
cases.stem: A toddler may have swallowed a grandparent's glipizide.

steps.q: Beyond dextrose, which antidote prevents repeated lows?

options.why: Blocks insulin release from the pancreas.

steps.q: Who do you call for help?

cases.pearl: **Sulfonylurea in a child: dextrose + octreotide, admit, call Poison Control.**
